candidates.source_summary: Plans for a direct rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again.
candidates.source_title: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to improve the rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again. Today, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays . Among those backing calls for the extra services was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who called Lumo’s bid to restore six daily direct services between Rochdale and the capital a “game-changing opportunity” for the borough and the wider North West. But the ORR rejected the plans after its assessment found adding more trains to the West Coast Main Line — which also included services to Blackpool and Wrexham — would likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers. It said its assessment following detailed and extensive analysis is that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the West Coast Main Line has not materially changed since it rejected a similar application by Lumo last year. An external review commissioned by ORR also supported this conclusion. READ MORE: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ The ORR said gaps in the current timetable need to provide important space for trains to recover when disruption occurs, minimising delays to passengers.

candidates.source_summary: Heywood and Middleton North MP Elsie Blundell has visited Redwood School’s sixth form campus at the Phoenix Centre in Heywood.
candidates.source_title: Heywood and Middleton North MP visits Redwood School’s sixth form at Phoenix Centre
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Heywood and Middleton North MP Elsie Blundell has visited Redwood School’s sixth form campus at the Phoenix Centre in Heywood. She met learners and staff to hear about their work supporting young people with special educational needs and disabilities. Ms Blundell said the teaching team was helping young people build skills and confidence for education, adult life and employment. Writing after the visit, she said “I’m so proud to have this facility - and the learners and parents - in my constituency.” Learners shared lessons with the MP during her visit, including the importance of recycling. Soup was also on the menu, with Ms Blundell describing it as “delicious” in her account of the visit. She thanked everyone at the campus for their welcome and the lessons they had shared. Ms Blundell also praised those involved in the sixth form’s work, writing “Well done again to the young people, parents, teachers and support staff.”

Attendees will receive a free will template, and refreshments will be available. Organisers say there is no obligation to take up further services. The clinic is open to people making their first will, considering changes to an existing one or seeking information about whether they need one. Charlotte Mascarenhas, supporter engagement fundraiser at Springhill Hospice, said “Taking your first steps to formalising your will can feel confusing, and some people don’t know where to start. Our Free Will Information Clinic is designed to make it all seem simpler.” Mr Copeland said Molesworths was waiving its usual fee in exchange for a donation to the hospice. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Dodgy frontman Nigel Clark will perform at St Chad’s Church in Rochdale on Friday 23 October, supported by Heywood singer-songwriter Grace Rose. The show runs from 5pm to 8pm, with tickets offered on a pay what you can basis. The performance is part of The Early Doors Club, which has expanded to Rochdale with funding from Greater Manchester Combined Authority’s Culture Fund. A stage, professional sound equipment and lighting have been installed at the town centre church for a series of live shows. An introductory event in September featured Liam Fender, supported by Rebecca Spooner. Clark is the frontman of Dodgy, whose hits include Good Enough and Staying Out for the Summer. Support act Grace Rose is 19 and from Heywood. The Early Doors Club is delivered by The Snug Coffee House in Atherton. It stages early evening performances in cafés, churches, community halls and heritage venues, with events finishing by 9pm. Organisers say the project has staged more than 160 events, attracted over 13,500 people and supported more than 250 artists since launching in 2023.

candidates.source_title: Fate of major housing scheme on playing fields in Bamford to be decided
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Developers want to build 450 houses on former playing fields in Rochdale . The fate of one of the initial phases of the giant scheme will be decided next week. In August, Rochdale council ’s planning committee delayed making a decision on Wain Home’s plan to build 45 houses on a plot of land behind Greenvale, in Bamford. The committee felt they didn’t have enough detail about drainage from the developers. The site, to the west of Norden Road, has a history of flooding. So the panel of councillors wanted to ensure proper precautions were being taken by the developer before making a decision. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter This scheme would be the first of many for the former green belt land – which contains a number of playing fields and sports pitches. The Bamford site was taken out of green belt status after the adoption of the Greater Manchester housing strategy named Places for Everyone. A new clubhouse for Bridge FC and revamped sports pitches within the site are seen as the major benefits that would come from the overarching scheme. The plan would see access created through the demolition of Chadwick Farm Barn on Greenvale. In its place a T-junction would provide vehicle access to the site. It wasn’t just flood risks that the planning committee took issue with. Objectors at the meeting on August 5 raised concern over there being no safeguarding set in stone for how transport connectivity, drainage, highways, and local amenities would work across the whole site. To get the very latest from Manchester's political scene in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Planning agent Gareth Salthouse, representing Wain Homes, explained that drainage for the site had been assessed and said this plan could be done quickly to bring ‘much-needed housing’ to the area. The planning committee was also concerned about the lack of overall masterplan. Coun Tom Besford feared this ‘piecemeal development’ would see each developer do the bare minimum of affordable homes for each plot on the land. He felt this would eventually result in all the benefits not coming to fruition. Coun Besford said: “Why would we go through the blood, sweat and tears of getting PfE over the line but then just give this land away. We have to assume that we could get 10 other plans like this. “Then what if it doesn’t add up and everything falls short overall.” The committee agreed to defer the decision based on questions over drainage. They will reconvene on Thursday, October 22 to make a final decision on the scheme.

candidates.source_summary: People are being urged to remain vigilant following several reports of calls involving scammers impersonating police officers to obtain personal and sensitive information linked to cryptocurrency.
candidates.source_title: Warning over scam callers impersonating police officers - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: People are being urged to remain vigilant following several reports of calls involving scammers impersonating police officers to obtain personal and sensitive information linked to cryptocurrency. Greater Manchester Police said one common method is to claim that they have arrested a suspect who was in possession of the victim’s personal documents, such as their passport, driving licence or banking details. On several occasions, fraudsters asked victims about their cryptocurrency accounts, specifically looking for their IDs, recovery phrases, and security codes. GMP says officers will never ask anyone to share this information or move your accounts. Police say the calls can appear convincing and are being made through spoofed GMP phone numbers. DS Reed, of GMP Cyber Crime Team, said: “These calls are an incredibly sophisticated type of crime, and those responsible are targeting our vulnerable communities. “We take offences of this nature incredibly seriously, and our team is working around the clock to understand how these offences have occurred, and how to prevent it from continuing. “Our officers will never get you to share security codes or personal information in relation to cryptocurrency, and if you are receiving calls that ask you to do so, please do not respond and report to us immediately.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale, which is set to become a nationally significant gateway driving the development of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster in the region. The 30,000 sq. ft centre is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub for advanced materials and manufacturing in Rochdale, bringing together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners in one location. AVID provides an environment where organisations can innovate, grow and commercialise new technologies, strengthening Greater Manchester’s position as a leading centre for advanced materials and manufacturing. Completion of the building represents a major milestone for years of partnership working between Rochdale Development Agency (RDA), Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners. RDA has led the physical development of the SMMC, working with partners to secure investment and position advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority opportunity for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The next phase will see work move from construction towards specialist fit-out ahead of bringing the centre into operation in 2027. The RDA brought together partners from industry, academia and government to establish the Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) in 2023. Since then, businesses have been able to connect with a national network of specialist expertise, facilities and innovation support through the CEAMS partners, including The University of Manchester, the Henry Royce Institute, National Physical Laboratory (NPL), Centre for Process Innovation (CPI) and NCC (formerly National Composites Centre). CEAMS has already supported more than 90 companies, developing new products and processes and demonstrating the value of a more connected innovation ecosystem.

I want to begin with Hopwood Hall. The council welcomed the recent High Court judgement, which found in our favour and brings much-needed clarity about the future of this important historic building. While it's disappointing that a lengthy and potentially costly legal process was necessary, we are now focused on moving forward. Since 2017, more than £1.6 million has been invested in Hopwood Hall by the council and Historic England, and we remain committed to funding essential repairs. Feasibility studies have been completed and options for its long-term future will be considered in due course. What is certain is that, once restored, Hopwood Hall will serve the wider Middleton community and continue to play an important role in the town's rich heritage. There has also been a significant boost for Middleton's regeneration ambitions, with a series of announcements demonstrating the momentum building behind the town's Mayoral Development Corporation. I'm delighted that Middleton Old Grammar School, recently acquired by the council, is expected to announce a new tenant before the end of the year. This follows news that the council is in the process of acquiring the long-derelict Warwick Mill, which could be brought back into productive use, including the potential development of new homes. Meanwhile, plans are progressing to transform Middleton Scout Hut into a vibrant community venue offering activities and training opportunities for young people. There is more good news on the horizon, with banking and post office services set to return to Middleton town centre in the new year. This is something I have long championed and it will provide another welcome boost for the town centre. These projects form part of our wider commitment to invest in every part of the borough, creating jobs, driving economic growth and ensuring our communities thrive. candidates.source_title: Huge queue as SpudBros launch Rochdale store - and delighted schoolgirl wins a trolley dash - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A queue of hungry punters headed out to Rochdale as SpudBros launched their latest new express store serving up their signature loaded jacket potatoes. With millions of followers on social media, the SpudBros phenomenon continues to grow with Lancashire brothers Jacob and Harley Nelson steering the expansion. The duo, who first started out with one tram on Preston's Flag Market, launched their 21st new SpudBros Express store in partnership with the EG station on Manchester New Road on Tuesday. Huge queues formed after the brothers announced the first 100 people would get a free spud on opening day. Not only that, but there was a special surprise awaiting the very first person in the queue - who was Rochdale schoolgirl Isla Lawrence. Click here for the latest on Manchester's food & drink scene, gigs and more in our CityLife newsletter 11-year-old Isla and mum Jackie had queued from 7am on the day to be the first served up a spud by Jacob and Harley themselves. But the five hour queue was to be worth it for Isla. As, after selecting her favourite toppings, Jacob then revealed to Isla she had won a trolley dash around the EG Spar shop to fill with anything she liked. It included the chance to win a "golden spud" which was hidden somewhere around the EG shop which would translate to a £100 cash prize. Isla had one minute to dash around the store, with Harley on hand to help with the trolley. But while she swiftly found the toy aisle and some of her favourite Squishy dumplings, the golden spud eluded the youngster. The brothers have announced the golden spud will now roll over to the next SpudBros Express store opening, which will be in Leicester, to become a £200 cash prize. Kind-hearted Isla though was happy with her trolley dash prizes - and even took her toy haul around to other children in the queue to share her prize, melting the hearts of Jacob and Harley. They said: "One of our missions is about giving back, and we want to inspire younger people so it was lovely to see her giving some of her prizes away." Isla's mum Jackie said: "She was so excited to come, she's been up since 4.30am. She's never been able to get to any of the SpudBros [events] before, but was so excited that this one was just down the road from us. She likes the SpudBros because they help people, and that's what she's done today by being generous with her prizes to people." The Rochdale SpudBros opening forms part of an ambitious nationwide expansion that will see 30 new roadside locations launch across EG on the Move forecourts over the next three years. The latest launch follows a rapid succession of SpudBros Express openings across Liverpool, Sheffield, Portsmouth, London, Edinburgh and Swindon alongside EG On The Move concessions in Blackburn, Wakefield, Barnstaple, Newcastle Upon Tyne, Wyberton, Nottingham, Chepstow, Prescot, Shrewsbury, Doncaster, Colne, Bolton , Birmingham and Aberdeen. The partnership marks SpudBros' first dedicated move into roadside and forecourt retail, taking its cult-favourite loaded spuds beyond traditional high streets and into one of the UK's busiest convenience channels. candidates.source_summary: A school is changing the way it celebrates success and achievements following concerns about innocent images of children being turned into sexualised content.
candidates.source_title: School to limit online images as AI manipulation threat rises - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A school is changing the way it celebrates success and achievements following concerns about innocent images of children being turned into sexualised content. The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) and the National Crime Agency (NCA) have seen a national increase in online offenders exploiting publicly available images of children to create realistic sexual content. The IWF found 3,440 AI-generated videos of child sexual abuse in 2025, compared to just 13 in 2024, and the NCA has increasingly seen offenders using AI technologies to target children in sinister new ways. Following updated guidance from both organisations, Cardinal Langley RC High School in Middleton says it will continue to celebrate achievements of students, but will make changes to reduce the risk of altered images. In a letter to parents, deputy headteacher Angela Williams said: “The dignity and wellbeing of every young person entrusted to our care sits at the heart of our safeguarding responsibilities. Those responsibilities also require us to respond when technology changes and new risks emerge. We are therefore making an important change to the way we use photographs of pupils online. “Artificial intelligence technology has developed extremely rapidly. One consequence is that an ordinary photograph placed on a website or social-media platform can potentially be copied and used by another person to create convincing AI altered imagery. The person in the original photograph does not need to have given permission and may have no knowledge that their image has been used. Cardinal Langley will look at different ways to celebrate students’ success “Recent national safeguarding guidance for education settings has consequently encouraged schools to reconsider how identifiable images of children and young people are made publicly available online.

candidates.source_summary: A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale.
candidates.source_title: New Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre takes shape in Rochdale - The Manufacturer
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major milestone has been reached for Atom Valley with completion of the base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale, which is set to become a nationally significant gateway driving the development of the advanced materials and manufacturing cluster in the region. The 30,000 sq. ft centre is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub for advanced materials and manufacturing in Rochdale, bringing together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners in one location. AVID provides an environment where organisations can innovate, grow and commercialise new technologies, strengthening Greater Manchester’s position as a leading centre for advanced materials and manufacturing. Completion of the building represents a major milestone for years of partnership working between Rochdale Development Agency (RDA), Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners. RDA has led the physical development of the SMMC, working with partners to secure investment and position advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority opportunity for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The next phase will see work move from construction towards specialist fit-out ahead of bringing the centre into operation in 2027. The RDA brought together partners from industry, academia and government to establish the Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) in 2023. Since then, businesses have been able to connect with a national network of specialist expertise, facilities and innovation support through the CEAMS partners, including The University of Manchester, the Henry Royce Institute, National Physical Laboratory (NPL), Centre for Process Innovation (CPI) and NCC (formerly National Composites Centre). CEAMS has already supported more than 90 companies, developing new products and processes and demonstrating the value of a more connected innovation ecosystem.

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale Council will apply new planning rules shifting more applications to officers and limiting committee referrals from October 31.
candidates.source_title: Rochdale Council Adopts New Planning Decision Rules - SuaraGarut.ID
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council is preparing to implement revised planning decision procedures from October 31, with more applications to be decided by planning officers rather than elected committees under new Government guidance for councils across England.The changes follow the Town and Country Planning Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions England Regulations 2026 and aim to allow committees to focus on major proposals while officers handle more routine cases, according to a council report.Under the new system, applications will be divided into two schedules. Schedule One cases, including householder applications, minor commercial and minor residential proposals, lawful development certificates and technical matters, must be determined by planning officers.Schedule Two applications can be referred to the planning committee, including larger developments, listed building consent, advertisement consent, tree preservation order consent and legal agreements with developers. However, referrals require agreement between a nominated councillor and nominated officer.A council report said the Government wants planning committees to have a clearer role focused on significant proposals while technical and smaller decisions are handled by officers."The Government’s aim is to provide greater clarity and consistency regarding the role of planning committees in decision-making, so that committees focus on key proposals that matter to an area while more minor and technical decisions are made by planning officers." said Rochdale Council in its report.The report also stated that councillors will still be able to engage with planning matters, raise residents’ concerns and submit material planning reasons. However, a councillor request alone will not require an application to be considered by the committee.Ward councillors will no longer be able to automatically call applications into committee meetings, and the previous threshold based on the number of objections received will also no longer trigger committee consideration.The council report warned that decisions could face legal challenges if a planning committee determines an application that regulations require officers to decide. Such decisions may be subject to judicial review and could be quashed.

candidates.source_summary: Changes to the way planning applications are decided across the borough will come into effect later this month.
candidates.source_title: Major changes to planning decisions are on the way - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Changes to the way planning applications are decided across the borough will come into effect later this month. From October 31, all councils must comply with new Government guidance required by the Town and Country Planning (Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions) (England) Regulations 2026. The aim is for planning officers to determine more applications, allowing planning committees to focus on larger applications and issues. One of the biggest changes is the designation of applications that must be determined by officers and cannot go before the committee. Applications that can be considered by the committee must be referred to it by a nominated councillor and council officer. And applications can no longer be automatically called-in by ward councillors, nor will there be a threshold for the number of objections received that will trigger a committee consideration. On Thursday, Rochdale Council is being asked to adopt the changes. A report to the council said: “The Government’s aim is to provide greater clarity and consistency regarding the role of planning committees in decision-making, so that committees focus on key proposals that matter to an area while more minor and technical decisions are made by planning officers. “Members may continue to engage with the planning process, raise residents’ concerns and submit material planning reasons. A member request will not itself require committee determination, but may be considered by the nominated member and nominated officer.”
